a fine-grain alluvial fan developed through a series of depositional environments, each with a different sediment source, that the rate of aggradation was not constant, that the succession of depositional regimes was controlled by the crossing of geomorphological thresholds and that climate change was not the primary control on aggradation.
a fine-grain alluvial fan developed through a sequence of depositional environments in response to aggradation alone.

the postglacial history of a fine-grain alluvial fan was conditioned by a succession of deposi- tional environments, each with a characteristic suite of sedimentary structures, grain size distribution, grain roundness distribution, loss on ignition distribution and charcoal abundance distribution, and that the succession of environments was conditioned by a sequence of threshold crossings, each triggered by a change in the balance of erosion, transport and deposition.
